restList.body:
BUTCHR-114 reviewing as instrument for BUTCHR-138 Arm C, review R1 at H1.

REVIEWED-SHA: af4a01cf4ca16040f79f86fad863d9640e003611

CHANGES_REQUESTED is requested here as an INSTRUMENT STATE, not as a criticism of this PR — there is nothing wrong with it. R1 exists to test whether CHANGES_REQUESTED freezes its recorded commit while APPROVED tracks the head. Throwaway; DO NOT MERGE. Verified: single new scratch file, 7 added lines; branch is 13 commits behind origin/main, so the step-4 base-merge to H4 will be a real merge.

The sha above is written into this body deliberately: the review body is one of the two candidate immutable records under test. R1's body is the most valuable one to re-read at T1, because if the body holds while .commit_id moves, that is a direct answer to Q2.

BUTCHR-114 reviewing as instrument for BUTCHR-138 Arm C, review R2 at H2.

REVIEWED-SHA: 199195819ff61e3c55b992ef484da4918baa0d38

Instrument approval on a throwaway measurement PR. DO NOT MERGE. R2 is the review that was intended to separate state from recency; note that under the two-condition rule now standing, R2's chain is already broken by the H1->H2 plain commit, so a null here is expected and is NOT evidence for recency.

The sha above is written into this body deliberately: the review body is the one record measured so far to hold immutably while .commit_id moves.

BUTCHR-114 reviewing as instrument for BUTCHR-138 Arm C, review R3 at H3.

REVIEWED-SHA: 652d1af2cec59e0b7ea73ab007dc1c5902069c41

Instrument approval on a throwaway measurement PR. DO NOT MERGE. Verified before approving: H3 is a single-parent plain commit on top of H2, which is what Arm C's design requires. R3 is the review whose chain will be intact when the step-4 base-merge lands, so R3 is the one expected to advance.

The sha above is in this body deliberately: the body is the one record measured so far to hold immutably while .commit_id moves.
